title: MyLoyal Activity Feed
subtitle: A persistent engagement surface for the MyLoyal app
summary: Push notifications die the moment they're swiped away. I'm designing a persistent 13-card activity feed, with carousel mechanics and a state machine, so quests, offers, and notifications have a place users can return to.

problem.statement: Push notifications died the moment users swiped them away. There was no in-app place to revisit them, and no ongoing engagement surface for quests or offers.
problem.bizCtx: Push was the only way MyLoyal users learned about offers and quests. Client brands wanted the app to feel alive, giving users a reason to open it beyond reacting to a push.
problem.constraints: Needed to support 13 distinct card types (notifications, quests, verification, rewards, among others) within a single carousel-based system, backed by a state machine to manage each card's lifecycle.

methods: Internal discussions on push limitations and engagement ideas

findings.finding: Dismissed notifications were gone for good
findings.evidence: Users had no in-app record of past push content once a notification was dismissed.
findings.implication: The feed had to persist notification content, not just quests and offers.

findings.finding: Engagement needed a home, not another one-off
findings.evidence: Quests, offers, and verification prompts were each candidates for their own surface.
findings.implication: Combine them into one card system instead of scattered features.

insight.decision: One persistent feed combining notifications, quests, and offers, built as a single card system: 13 card types sharing one state machine and one card anatomy, instead of one-off implementations per type.

design.solution: A carousel-based activity feed supporting 13 card types (including notifications, quests, verification, and rewards), each managed through a shared state machine.
design.flows: Users see active cards in a horizontal carousel, tap into a card to take action or view more detail, and cards update or clear based on the state machine as actions are completed.
design.annotations: A horizontal carousel won over other layouts because it surfaces cards without displacing the home screen's existing elements. The state machine is deliberately generic: no one-off logic per card type.

outcome.shipped: Still in development. The full card system, state machine, and carousel interaction have been designed.
outcome.measures: Not shipped yet; the measures the design should be held against once live: feed open rate, cards engaged per session, quest completion rate, and whether users return to re-read notification content they'd dismissed.
outcome.learnings: Designing one state machine flexible enough to support 13 different card types took more iteration than expected. Once the shared structure was right, adding new card types became much easier.
